# Enzyme release notes - v0.13.1

## Short version

Search and the map hold up on very large vaults. Keyword search now finds a
note by its frontmatter title and by the people, projects, and accounts it
links in frontmatter. `enzyme petri --query` stays fast at hundreds of
thousands of documents, and catalyst generation no longer fails on vaults with
very many notes. `catalyze --candidates N` adds an optional compact list of
further matches, and custom reading profiles now control the voice of the
questions they generate.

## What shipped

### Search

- Keyword search reads each note's title and frontmatter wikilinks along with
  its path, so a note that names a person, account, or project only in a field
  such as `people: ["[[Sam Rivera]]"]`, or whose title lives only in
  frontmatter, is found by that name. Results still report the note's path, and
  chunk text and embeddings are unchanged. (`298877b`)
- `catalyze --candidates N` (and the MCP tool's `candidates` parameter) lists up
  to N further notes after the full results, one line each: path, date, and a
  snippet around the first query term. They come from deeper pools (200 notes
  per side, 3,000 keyword chunks) fused the same way, so an agent can see notes
  ranked below the usual cut without reading full passages. The full results
  are unchanged, and pulling deeper adds no measurable time. Off by default.
  (`2f82f30`)
- On a ~512K-document test corpus, the top 10 results were identical with and
  without the flag for all 470 test questions, and the note a question needed
  was within reach (results plus candidates) for 420 of them, against at most
  394 before.

### The map on large vaults

- `petri --query` no longer reads document text or whole occurrence rows to
  rank entities. Two covering indexes, on entity occurrences (entity, weight)
  and on documents (path, modified time), keep both reads small. On a
  ~512K-document vault a call fell from 62–91 s to 4.0 s cold and 2.7 s warm,
  with an identical map. (`c2db252`)

### Catalyst generation

- Looking up chunks for many notes at once no longer fails on vaults with more
  paths than SQLite allows in one statement (32,766 by default); paths are
  looked up in batches with the same ordering. (`aeb2453`)
- Under custom reading profiles, the question format no longer requires first
  person: the profile sets the voice and person. A profile written for a team
  or company archive can ask third-person retrieval questions. Built-in
  profiles are unchanged. (`401ad50`)
- `enzyme dump-prompts` shows the excerpt limits hosted generation uses (up to
  40 per entity) instead of the local-model limit of 10. (`3feb7d2`)

## Behavior changes to check

- Existing vaults add the new indexes on the first read-write open after
  upgrading. This takes seconds on typical vaults and about a minute at
  half a million documents, once.
- Titles and frontmatter wikilinks enter the keyword index as notes are
  re-indexed. Notes that have not changed since the last `refresh` keep their
  old index entries until they are re-indexed.
